definitions.explanation: A formal kimono with very long, flowing sleeves, traditionally worn by young unmarried women on ceremonial occasions such as Coming of Age Day and weddings.

examples.japanese: {成人式|せいじんしき}に{振袖|ふりそで}を{着|き}る。
examples.english: To wear a furisode at the Coming of Age ceremony.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{振袖|ふりそで}を{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ。
{振袖|ふりそで}のレンタルは{予約|よやく}が{早|はや}いほど{良|よ}い{柄|がら}が{選|えら}べる。
examples.english: The earlier you book a furisode rental, the better the patterns you can choose from.

notes:
Composed of {振|ふ}る (to swing, wave) + {袖|そで} (sleeve). The name refers to the long, swinging sleeves that can reach 100-115 cm in length. The most formal type of kimono for young unmarried women.

TYPES BY SLEEVE LENGTH:
- {大振袖|おおふりそで}: the longest sleeves (~115 cm), most formal
- {中振袖|ちゅうふりそで}: medium-length sleeves (~100 cm)
- {小振袖|こふりそで}: shorter sleeves (~75 cm), less formal

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {振袖|ふりそで}を{着|き}る: to wear a furisode
- {振袖|ふりそで}のレンタル: furisode rental
- {振袖|ふりそで}{姿|すがた}: the appearance of someone in a furisode

CULTURAL NOTE:
Most commonly worn at {成人式|せいじんしき} (Coming of Age Day, January), where twenty-year-old women celebrate adulthood. Also worn by young women attending weddings as guests. After marriage, women traditionally switch to {留袖|とめそで} (short-sleeved formal kimono). Many families rent rather than purchase {振袖|ふりそで} due to the high cost.
